newsitem.title: USA: CME Nov lumber dips initially, rallies to new high.
newsitem.headline: CME Nov lumber dips initially, rallies to new high.

text.p: CME lumber futures opened lower paced by November, but rallied in early trade to post a new contract high in that month on continued strong fundamentals, traders said.

November fell as much as $6.50 per thousand board feet in initial trade and then rallied to trade up $0.50 at $484.20 at 0936 CST, a new contract high. Other months were up $1.70 to $4.40 with January up $1.70 at $419.00 per tbf.
Profit taking and speculative long liquidation weighed on November at the start. Prices then rose on continued support from a record high cash price market, traders said.
Deferred contracts also rose on short covering after sharp setbacks in those months late last week, they said.
Cash markets will likely provide little direction due to holidays in both the United States and Canada.
Oriented strand board traded lower in light early dealings, posting losses of $2.90 to $1.00 per 1,000 square feet (msf).
Both futures markets will close at 1200 CST due to the U.S. Veterans Day holiday.
